title: Create a Collaborative Project Team Environment
coreMove: A team proves collaboration when pressure rises by surfacing hidden signals, naming owners, and letting trust and working agreements shape the next delivery choice.

exampleSpecs.audience: project leads who need hard news to move through informal channels
exampleSpecs.stakes: a risk stays private while the official update remains falsely calm
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A brief chat turns a hidden schedule concern into a visible team signal.

exampleSpecs.stakes: the team may defend a clean chart instead of addressing the risk it hides
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A routine reporting move is interrupted and restarted around the hidden risk.

exampleSpecs.audience: quality leads building practical norms before a review
exampleSpecs.stakes: a defect concern may stay unspoken if the route for raising it is unclear
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A small physical detail shows how team norms make quality concerns speakable.

exampleSpecs.audience: procurement leads reconstructing why a warning did not travel
exampleSpecs.stakes: the same supplier exposure will recur if the team misreads the failure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The postmortem locates the missing tradeoff record as the decisive misstep.

exampleSpecs.audience: stakeholder-facing leads who soften signals under pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: support concerns may vanish from the rollout record
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The protagonist notices her own smoothing and corrects the signal before it disappears.

exampleSpecs.audience: delivery managers who need collaboration to survive after the meeting
exampleSpecs.stakes: a pressured choice may lose the reason it was made
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A written decision record carries the collaborative evidence and owner.
